Research program at HKUST

Listening to pipes to find leaks and blockages before they fail.

A theme based research program at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, developing methodologies to assist the design, operation, monitoring, and diagnostic repair of aging urban water supply systems.

About the research

Why aging water networks need a new way to be heard

Urban water supply systems age underground, out of sight. SMART UWSS develops the methodologies to design, operate, monitor, and diagnostically repair those systems, with research that could potentially benefit 3 billion people globally.

The problem. Pressurised pipelines carry a city’s water supply, but leaks and blockages inside them are hard to find without digging or shutting the network down. The program studies the waves that already travel through water filled pipes, and turns them into a diagnostic tool.

The approach. Using time reversal of acoustic waves, together with low frequency and high frequency wave methods and ambient noise measurement, the team works on detecting defects in pressurised pipelines and on monitoring large scale water supply networks in real time.

The setting. SMART UWSS is based at HKUST, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. The work is supported by the Hong Kong government and forms part of Hong Kong’s Water Intelligent Network (WIN) directive.

Technology

Time reversal acoustics for defect detection

The program’s core technique records acoustic waves in a pipe, time reverses them, and uses the refocused signal to detect and locate defects in pressurised pipelines.

Time reversal of acoustic waves in pipes

Time reversal (TR) of acoustic waves in pipes is the program’s central method for defect detection in pressurised pipelines. By reversing recorded wave signals and sending them back through the pipe, the energy refocuses at the defect, making leaks and blockages detectable and locatable.

Low frequency and high frequency waves

The research works across low frequency (LF) and high frequency (HF) waves. Work on LF TR and HF TR runs in parallel, and high frequency time reversal supports high resolution acoustic imaging of pressurised pipelines.

Ambient noise measurement and characterisation

Alongside active testing, the program measures and characterises ambient noise in water pipelines, and is developing time reversal using ambient noise. Work on TR using ambient noise is in preparation.

Automatic real time detection and distributed monitoring

The program is building an automatic real time system for defect detection at LF and HF, together with a distributed data acquisition system for monitoring and diagnosis of large scale water supply networks.

Network monitoring and diagnosis

A distributed data acquisition system for monitoring and diagnosis of large scale water supply networks.

How a detection runs

Four stages, one continuous listen. Watch the sequence run.

  1. 01

    Record

    Data acquisition points capture the acoustic waves already travelling through the pressurised, water filled pipe.

  2. 02

    Reverse

    The recorded signal is time reversed and sent back through the same pipe.

  3. 03

    Refocus

    The returning wave energy refocuses at the point where the pipe’s behaviour changes.

  4. 04

    Locate

    The refocused signal reveals the defect, a leak or a blockage, and where it sits in the network.
